newsitem.title: CHINA: Cheung Kong makes lucrative move into Hongkong Land.
newsitem.headline: Cheung Kong makes lucrative move into Hongkong Land.

text.p: Hong Kong tycoon Li Ka-shing has made a savvy move into Hongkong Land Holdings Ltd, building up a lucrative short-term investment which has potential for the long term without requiring a takeover, analysts said on Wednesday.
"As a stock investment it is already very good," said Vincent Luk, an analyst at HSBC James Capel. "Long term it is going to be a good asset. It's win-win all round."

Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday that Li's flagship company Cheung Kong and its Hutchison Whampoa Ltd unit together held a 3.03 percent stake in Jardine Matheson and a 3.06 percent stake in Hongkong Land.

Cheung Kong spokesman Kenneth Yuen said the group had begun to build up the stake "years ago", buying shares in the open market. "It was just normal buying for investment. As you know Cheung Kong has a portfolio of shares and investments," he said.

Yuen declined to say whether the Cheung Kong group would increase its stake, but speculation about a hostile takeover bid has given both Hongkong Land and Jardine Matheson shares a huge boost, leaving Li sitting on a hefty profit already.
Hongkong Land shares surged 22 percent in Singapore on Tuesday and another nine percent on Wednesday. Jardine Matheson rose 11 percent on Tuesday and five percent on Wednesday.
Both stocks have performed poorly since their Hong Kong listings were withdrawn, Jardine Matheson at the end of 1994 and Hongkong Land in March 1995.
"Maybe Li saw that there was very good value there," said Credit Suisse First Boston analyst Geoffrey Palmer.
Analysts said Li had seized the opportunity to buy into Hongkong Land's portfolio in Hong Kong's Central business district at a 40 percent discount to net asset value.
Hongkong Land is the largest landlord in Central.

Rather than a takeover bid, analysts said they expected future cooperation between the groups, with Cheung Kong holding little in terms of an office portfolio and Hongkong Land lacking on the development portfolio side.
"Cheung Kong gains probably the best property portfolio in Hong Kong. By taking a three percent stake, they are buying into the best quality commercial portfolio," said Palmer.

"I am sure that the Jardine group is happy to have such a shareholder behind them. Li Ka-shing has phenomenally good contacts and it would get rid of the colonial sort of overhang Jardine has," he added.

Merrill Lynch said there were synergies to be gained between the Cheung Kong group, which includes Hutchison Whampoa, Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd and Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd and Hongkong Land's burgeoning infrastructure investments in China and the region.

Hongkong Land's investment landbank of more than six million square feet was four times than of Cheung Kong's 1.4 million sq ft, allowing Cheung Kong to potentially lift its recurring income base by about two percent to 27 percent, Merrill added.
It said a takeover attempt was unlikely.

Following an unsuccessful raid on Hongkong Land by Cheung Kong and other Hong Kong blue chips in 1987, Jardine rearranged its structure. The group owns about 32 percent of Hongkong Land through Jardine Strategic Holdings (JSH) Ltd.
"The only way that control could be passed on would be in the event of JSH voting in favour of a third party general offer. This seems extremely unlikely," Merrill Lynch said.

"The most likely scenario, in our view, is that the acquisition of the three percent stakes is little more than astute treasury management from the Cheung Kong group with a possibility of closer cooperation between the two groups in the future," Merrill Lynch said.
